chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked him in the Sacred Mosque, 'Who is the greatest of people in burden (of sin)?' He said: 'The one who stands at these two stations, Arafat and Muzdalifah, and performs Sa'ee between these two mountains, then performs Tawaf by this House, and prays behind the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), then says to himself or thinks that Allah has not forgiven him, so he is from the people with the greatest burden.'

key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَةِ: Muzdalifah, the second major station of Hajj
key_terms.سَعَى: Sa'ee, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.ظَنَّ: to think or suppose (often implying doubt or assumption)
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: Arafat, the primary station of Hajj

ai.seo_question: Who is considered to have the greatest burden of sin in Islam according to Hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the person with the greatest burden of sin as one who performs the major rituals of Hajj correctly but falls into the trap of despair, thinking that Allah has not forgiven him despite his deeds. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'husn al-zann' (good opinion of God), where doubting divine mercy after fulfilling obligations is considered a greater sin than the omission of the rituals themselves, as it negates the spiritual fruit of the act.
